title: Clarify and tighten source-bundle permission granularity
description:
Problem: MCP source bridge tools are labeled SensitiveRead and are separately gated through CanReadSourceBundle, but the current permission mapper grants ReadSourceBundle to Viewer roles. Because the default configuration uses Auth:AnonymousAccess=Viewer, a signed-out local caller can satisfy the source-bundle policy after normal view access is allowed. That may be intentional for local-first development, but it is too implicit for a tool class that can resolve source-linked local file slices.

Evidence from the 2026-05-25 deepdive:
- MemorySmith.App/Services/SecurityServices.cs Allows() returns true for Viewer when permission is View, UseChat, or ReadSourceBundle.
- MemorySmith.App/appsettings.json defaults MemorySmith:Auth:AnonymousAccess to Viewer.
- MemorySmith.App/Controllers/McpController.cs gates ChatToolRisk.SensitiveRead through CanReadSourceBundleAsync.
- README.md and Data/Pages/features/api-and-mcp.md document source_bundle/find_by_source as SensitiveRead/source-bundle policy tools, but do not spell out that Viewer/anonymous Viewer currently satisfies that policy.

Desired outcome: make the source-bundle trust boundary explicit and least-surprising. Either keep Viewer access as an intentional local-first policy with docs/tests that state it clearly, or split source-bundle permission away from default Viewer/anonymous access so only Editor/Admin or a dedicated source-read grant can call source file tools.

Scope:
- In scope: role/permission decision, docs matrix update, regression tests for anonymous Viewer, authenticated Viewer, Editor, Admin, API-key, and auth-disabled behavior.
- In scope: compatibility notes for local development and MCP clients.
- Out of scope: making source tools chat-requestable or redesigning source-link allow/deny root enforcement.

Acceptance criteria:
- The intended CanReadSourceBundle role mapping is written in README or Data/Pages/features/api-and-mcp.md.
- Tests prove the chosen behavior for anonymous Viewer and authenticated Viewer callers.
- SensitiveRead naming, policy behavior, and operator docs no longer leave the role grant implicit.
- If Viewer access is retained, the docs explain the local-first risk and how to disable anonymous/source access.

Validation:
- Run targeted security/MCP tests covering source-bundle authorization.
- Run ./Scripts/Test-PageLinks.ps1 and ./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after doc/task changes.

comments.body: Created during 2026-05-25 deepdive audit after tracing SensitiveRead MCP source tools through McpController.CanReadSourceBundleAsync and SecurityServices.Allows. This is related to TSK-0151's documentation/test matrix, but specifically tracks whether Viewer/anonymous Viewer should satisfy source-bundle reads.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Tightened source-bundle authorization so Viewer no longer satisfies ReadSourceBundle. Source-bundle tools now require Editor/Admin, configured API-key access, or auth-disabled local installs; anonymous Viewer and authenticated Viewer callers are denied before SensitiveRead MCP tools execute. Updated README and api-and-mcp docs to make the boundary explicit. Validation: focused MCP SensitiveRead authorization tests passed 2/2.
